solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush to get paper first in holiday accommodation maybe

indicators.note: first says the paper's name is put at the front, before the word for rush

parts.note: The Times is a British national newspaper
to hare is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to grab a newspaper before checking into their holiday lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared-ownership holiday property, used by each owner for set weeks, is one example of holiday lodging; hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Country — it's upset, having taken gamble

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset says the little word it is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: A nation is in turmoil after staking money on a risky wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A Himalayan region, often called a country, now governed by China.

clue.text: Explosive megaton produced by machine

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters of megaton are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A huge nuclear blast is generated by some device.
explanation.definitionFit: A small electrical generator using permanent magnets, as once used in engine ignition, is a machine.

clue.text: Jerky old man aboard ship, up-to- date one, 100

indicators.note: aboard says the father figure is placed within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
old man is slang for father, pa
mod means modern, up to date
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A list of jerky things: an old man on a ship, something modern, one hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' is the container signal: the old man sits inside the ship, the usual crossword sense of being on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic movement comes in sudden irregular bursts, so jerky is a synonym.

clue.text: Old natives in deep pit, involved with a sin that's terrible

parts.note: an abyss is a bottomless pit

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of in and a sin are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Ancient peoples have been thrown into a deep pit for some awful wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' just joins the pit to the anagram; IN plus A SIN rearranged gives INIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the old name for Ethiopia, so its people were the old natives of that land.

clue.text: Some damsel meandering in wood

indicators.note: some says only part of the words that follow is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A young woman is wandering about in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is a hardwood timber as well as the tree, so a type of wood.

clue.text: Records debate in which US doesn't participate

indicators.note: doesn't participate says the letters U and S drop out of the word for debate

parts.note: to discuss is to debate
US is taken as written

explanation.surface: A political argument goes ahead without America taking part, and it gets recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Gramophone records are flat discs, so records is a synonym.

clue.text: Greek party, endlessly sumptuous

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for sumptuous is cut off

parts.note: rich means sumptuous, lavish

explanation.surface: A Greek celebration goes on and on in great luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical Greek orders of architecture and a dialect of ancient Greek, so it means Greek.

clue.text: Ostentatiously display message disappointing those hoping to see musical?

definitions.meaning: to flaunt or parade something before others

definitions.text: message disappointing those hoping to see musical?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a notice saying the show is cancelled, bad news for theatregoers

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to flaunt; split up it is the notice that a performance is cancelled.

clue.text: What sounds like cunning experiment is most trivial

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken like the phrase for a cunning experiment

parts.note: sly means cunning and a test is an experiment

explanation.surface: A crafty scientific trial is dismissed as of very little importance.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of slight, meaning least significant, so most trivial.

clue.text: Poor woman happy to be in seaside location?

indicators.note: to be in says the word for happy is placed inside the seaside spot

parts.note: a bay is a stretch of coast
glad means happy

explanation.surface: A woman enjoys being at the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeless woman carrying her belongings in bags is a poor woman.

clue.text: Engineer to study electrical current after damage

indicators.note: after says the study and current come behind the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage
to con is to study, as in con a text
I is the physics symbol for current

explanation.surface: An engineer studies an electrical current after something has been damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian engineer who pioneered radio.

clue.text: The member abandoning a unit

indicators.note: abandoning says the letter A is left out of the word for member

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club member walks out on one unit of the organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat, equal to 100,000 British thermal units, used for gas billing.

clue.text: Get rid of idiot, loth ultimately to show sign of penance

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss, get rid of
a clot is a fool

indicators.note: ultimately says only the final letter of loth is used

explanation.surface: A manager reluctantly fires a fool as an act of repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse sacking cloth was worn, often with ashes, to show remorse, a sign of penance.

clue.text: Something cheesy, funny act? One can't stop smiling

parts.note: Cheshire is a crumbly English cheese

indicators.note: funny says the letters of act are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A corny comic routine, and someone who keeps grinning.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England giving its name to a cheese. 'funny' rearranges ACT to CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The grinning cat in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, proverbial for a fixed broad smile.

clue.text: Aussie animal to burrow in ground endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for burrowing is dropped

parts.note: to root is to dig, as a pig roots in the soil

explanation.surface: An Australian creature digs into the earth without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for a kangaroo, an Australian marsupial.

clue.text: Where Aaron Lennon would play as one of the Blues?

definitions.meaning: Aaron Lennon was an English footballer, a winger on the right flank
the Blues are Britain's Conservatives, whose colour is blue, on the political right

explanation.walkthrough: Aaron Lennon played wide right for Tottenham and England; British Conservatives are known as the Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballing position on the right flank, and a political leaning towards conservatism.

clue.text: Author providing ideal end destroyed enemy

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of ideal end are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A writer gives a perfect finish to a ruined enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEAL END rearranged gives DANIEL DE, then FOE: the author of Robinson Crusoe, spelt with E where the grid prints A.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: The German admits making mistake providing weapon

indicators.note: admits says the word for making a mistake is let inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
erring means making a mistake

explanation.surface: A German confesses to a blunder concerning a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small short-barrelled pocket pistol, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Great search organised to find intruder

indicators.note: organised says the letters of great search are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A big hunt is mounted to track down a trespasser.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up at a party uninvited is an intruder.

clue.text: Sailor carries sheep around in vehicle

indicators.note: carries says the sailor's word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: tar is old slang for a sailor
a ram is a male sheep
C is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: A seaman transports a sheep in some vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram running on street rails is a passenger vehicle.

clue.text: Boat heads west in sort of canal

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: a tug is a small powerful boat

explanation.surface: A boat travels westward along a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The alimentary canal is the digestive tract, so the intestine is a sort of canal.

clue.text: European in work unit set up explosive device

indicators.note: in a down clue set up says the whole is turned upwards, read backwards
in says the European goes inside the unit of work

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
a Dane is a European

explanation.surface: A European in a work team puts together a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the whole assembly, since in a down clue raising it means reading from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand-thrown bomb is an explosive device.

clue.text: One comes across wild folk invading territory

indicators.note: invading says the wild folk go inside the abbreviation for territory

parts.note: Ter. is an abbreviation for territory
ravers are wild partygoers

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses over as wild people invade some land.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who traverses something crosses it, so one who comes across.

clue.text: Like Napoleon once on foreign island

parts.note: ex means former, once
île is French for island

explanation.surface: Napoleon was formerly on a foreign island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Napoleon was banished to Elba and then St Helena.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished, so he was a banished person, one like him.

clue.text: Some complainer that's disinclined to do anything

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A grumbler who won't lift a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means sluggish and inactive, unwilling to move.

clue.text: Time and time again includes a brief message

indicators.note: includes says the two time letters hold the word for brief between them

parts.note: a second T for time
wee means small or brief

explanation.surface: Over and over again, someone sends a short message.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post on the social network formerly called Twitter is a message.

clue.text: Slant of glib talk by trendy Conservative

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a line is smooth persuasive patter

explanation.surface: A trendy Tory's smooth patter has a certain bias.
explanation.definitionFit: An incline is a slope, so a slant.

clue.text: Aim to be here

definitions.meaning: this entry sits at the bottom of the grid and its clue word is last, at the finish

explanation.definitionFit: An end is a goal; it is also the finishing point where this clue is placed.

clue.text: Firm taking a gent inappropriately from the same family

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: inappropriately says the letters of a gent are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A company hires a man unsuitably, perhaps a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related by descent, sharing a common origin, as words or kin.

clue.text: Mad king? Not the first leader of England in deep depression

indicators.note: not the first says the first E in the king's name goes, the earlier of the two

parts.note: George III was the British king famous for his madness

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of England

explanation.surface: A mad king, not the first ruler of England, sinks into depression.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a deep narrow ravine, a depression in the land, not a mood.

clue.text: Feature of dishwashing to put fellow off

parts.note: to put off, with off coming after fellow, means to deter
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A dishwashing feature might put a man off.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up liquid or dishwasher tablets are detergent, a key part of dishwashing.
